first_impression.reaction: Googled 'crete wedding packages' because Crete is on our maybe list next to Santorini. The opener, 'Two Crete wedding packages can carry the same name and share almost nothing on paper.', is the problem I actually have, not a sunset. Then it lists exactly where they part ways: rooms, sole use, reception, extra hours, suppliers. No 'dream day' in sight. Kept reading.

journey.section: What a Crete wedding package covers
journey.quote: Abaton's packages run from a minimum reception of 20 guests to a maximum of 300, Grecotel Amirandes near Heraklion hosts weddings for up to 300 guests, and Avra Imperial in Kolymvari has an events hall it says holds up to 680 people.
journey.reaction: Right at the top, proof Crete can take 60 to 90 people. That's my first filter and it's answered in the first scroll. Good.

journey.section: Resort packages with a minimum stay
journey.quote: Its packages are valid with a minimum booking of 10 rooms for at least two nights, depending on guest numbers, and they do not include the accommodation itself.
journey.reaction: That's the kind of condition you only find out on email three. Rooms are a condition but not included. Exactly the hidden-cost trap I'm worried about.

journey.quote: On the day, it covers two witnesses if needed, a ceremony set-up with seasonal flowers, a bouquet and boutonniere, a pre-recorded playlist, champagne while getting ready and a short fireworks display, followed by champagne breakfast in bed.
journey.reaction: Around here I started skimming. Elounda, Nana Princess, Euphoria's three tiers, Out of the Blue, Minoa: lots of item-by-item lists. I don't need every bouquet. Tell me what's different.

journey.quote: Deluxe Dream includes welcome drinks of homemade lemonade and berry water, champagne and chocolate strawberries in the honeymoon suite, and an event coordinator present throughout the stay.
journey.reaction: 'Deluxe Dream' and chocolate strawberries is exactly the resort-package vibe we're trying to avoid. That's the venue's naming, not the article's, but it tells me a venue package alone won't feel like us.

journey.quote: It records an informal ceremony, not a legal marriage.
journey.reaction: Blunt and useful. Mum would have assumed a certificate means married. Glad it's spelled out.

journey.section: Are Crete wedding packages all inclusive?
journey.quote: The phrase "all inclusive" on a Crete resort usually describes the holiday, not the wedding.
journey.reaction: Honest. That one line saves a misunderstanding with my parents, who are paying 40 percent and will read 'all inclusive' literally.

journey.quote: Out of the Blue settles registry office fees inside its Civil and Orthodox packages, so the same question has two different answers on one island.
journey.reaction: This is the honest trade-off stuff I want. Shows someone actually compared the fine print rather than pasting brochures.

journey.section: Venue package, venue fee or a planner
journey.quote: A planner connects the venue, suppliers and guests into one plan, but adds another party to brief and another agreement to read closely.
journey.reaction: A planning company admitting a planner has a downside. That reads fair, not salesy. I still want to know what 'connects' means for us in practice, but the list is honest.

journey.section: East or west Crete for a package wedding
journey.quote: Between them, around Heraklion, sit Out of the Blue at Aghia Pelaghia, Nana Princess at Chersonissos and Grecotel Amirandes, which is 15 minutes from Heraklion International Airport.
journey.reaction: Fifteen minutes from the airport is the grandparents answer. I wanted that for every cluster: which airport do guests fly into for the west and the east, and how long is the drive? The section raises it then leaves me to work it out.

journey.section: How to compare two Crete quotes like for like
journey.quote: Level access. Can older guests reach the ceremony and reception without steps or sand, and is there an accessible bathroom nearby?
journey.reaction: Steps or sand. That's someone who's watched a grandmother on a beach ceremony. This whole checklist, the weather plan and the contract language too, goes to James tonight.

journey.quote: How far could the exchange rate move the total between deposit and balance, and who carries that risk?
journey.reaction: My number one fear, named properly. Dad will want this list.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=crete-wedding-packages&utm_content=primary) whether you already hold quotes or are still shaping your shortlist.
journey.reaction: AUD and in writing is a real plus, and 'still shaping your shortlist' is us, so it doesn't feel like it's only for people further along. Small snag: Advisor, then Concierge in the same sentence. Is that one person or two services?

unanswered_questions: For 60 to 90 guests with half flying in from Australia, which Crete corner would you actually steer us toward, east, west or around Heraklion?
Which airport would guests use for the Chania resorts versus Elounda, and roughly how long is the transfer?
Who gets our guests, including grandparents, from the airport to the venue?
Who is on the ground on the day if something goes wrong: our Wedded Advisor, someone you are accountable for, or the venue's coordinator?
Is there a real Crete wedding you've planned, with venue and date, that we can look at?
would_share_with: James (partner): the quote comparison checklist, to send identical questions to each venue
Mum and Dad (contributing): the 'all inclusive' section and the currency, deposit and insurance questions
Both sets of parents: the legal section and the symbolic versus legal explanation

cta_reaction.quote: When your shortlist is ready, [plan your Crete wedding with the Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=crete-wedding-packages&utm_content=closing), or return to [our curated Greece wedding collection](https://weddedwonderland.com/destinations/europe/greece).
cta_reaction.why: Calm, not pushy, and AUD quotes in writing speak to my biggest fear. But we haven't chosen a country yet, and I'd want two more posts and one real wedding before handing over our details.

top_3_changes: Trim the venue-by-venue inclusion lists (Elounda Lavish on the day, Nana Princess tiers, Euphoria's three tiers, Minoa Palace) to what actually differs between them; the comparisons are the valuable part, not every bouquet and strawberry.

In the east or west section, give guests' arrival point for each cluster the way Amirandes gets '15 minutes from Heraklion International Airport', so a couple with older guests can judge transfers by corner.
Make the Wedded Advisor and Wedded Concierge relationship clear in the primary CTA and closing, so it is obvious whether we'd be speaking to one person or booking two services.

checks.check: Every journey point and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Every turn-off has a why (none found; not invented)
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie (planner_couple), using persona voice and concerns
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and VERIFY markers ignored
Title, business details and absent prices treated as not must-fix; no requests for sourcing or not-published lines

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'crete wedding packages' during early destination research, about 14 months out.
Skimmed the venue inclusion lists; read the all-inclusive, left-out, comparison, legal and Australian sections closely.
No prices appear by design, so the 'vague pricing' turn-off was not raised.
Transfers, on-the-day accountability and real weddings are deferred business details, listed as unanswered questions only and not as must-fix.
Venue-supplied names and wording (e.g. 'Deluxe Dream', chocolate strawberries) were not counted as brand cliché turn-offs.
The persona card is provisional (not CRM-calibrated).
